title: Introducing The Information's 50 Most Promising Startups of 2026
summary: The Information released its annual list of 50 promising early-stage startups, selected on revenue, business models and growth prospects, and for the first time added a dedicated security category. Three of the four most highly valued companies on the list are security startups worth more than $1 billion, and named picks include AI penetration-testing firm Tenzai, Nir Zuk's newly founded Cylake and Noitom Robotics. The publication notes past picks such as Cursor's maker, chosen at a $400 million valuation and later acquired by SpaceX for $60 billion.

title: Jensen Huang's Downfall
summary: WSJ Technology's weekly lead recaps Jensen Huang's rapid exit from Nvidia: within a week he acknowledged an affair with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of passing information to Chinese intelligence, a second affair with a longtime Nvidia executive triggered an emergency board meeting, and he resigned with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO. The piece adds WSJ reporting that in his final months Huang clashed with Kress over Nvidia's use of its balance sheet to support cloud startups and backstop data-center projects, warning that an "avalanche" of purchase commitments threatened the company. Investors will hear from Kress when Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday.

title: What It Takes to Deliver Your Wings Order During a Football Game, Fast and Hot
summary: The Wall Street Journal looks at how Wingstop relies on its digital ordering infrastructure, with a single order potentially drawing on about 40 different Amazon Web Services cloud services. Nearly 74% of the chain's third-quarter restaurant sales came through its app and online delivery and pickup channels, making fast, reliable technology central to its business during demand spikes such as football games.

title: How Jensen Huang Built the Backdoor Route That Keeps Beijing in the AI Race
summary: The Wall Street Journal examines how large data centers in Southeast Asia, built with Nvidia's cooperation under Jensen Huang, supplied crucial computing power to Chinese companies despite U.S. export controls. The report says these facilities also served as cover for alleged smuggling of restricted chips, adding a national-security dimension to the scandal surrounding Huang's departure.

title: Nvidia CEO Ouster Reverberates Globally
summary: Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO is rippling through the chip sector, AI startups and U.S.-China relations, as workarounds that let Chinese buyers access Nvidia chips may now close and the company's role as a funder of smaller AI firms shrinks. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the board to pick an outside CEO, while the FT reported Huang has privately discussed a return and the board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas. Interim CEO Colette Kress faces her first earnings call on Tuesday after the stock fell 13% last week.

title: The Investors Set to Win Big in Anthropic's IPO
summary: Anthropic's IPO this week is expected to value the Claude developer at $1.33 trillion or more, setting up large payouts for its more than 300 investors, from early angels in its 2021 Series A at a $461 million valuation to backers of its $965 billion Series H in May. The Information expects strong demand to push pricing above the $70–$78 preliminary range and a first-day open potentially well above $100 a share.

title: Nvidia's Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered
summary: Nvidia's role as a major investor in AI startups and cloud partners is expected to shrink under interim CEO Colette Kress, after Huang had already told cloud partners they would need upfront customer payments to get GPUs. UBS estimates the pullback could remove $50 billion or more from the market, with pending deals involving Reflection AI and a planned investment in Thinking Machines Lab at a $40 billion valuation in doubt.

title: Trump Administration to Name Nvidia Among AI 'National Champions'
summary: The Trump administration plans to designate more than two dozen companies, including Nvidia, as AI 'national champions' to spread U.S. AI technology abroad. The designation brings faster export-license approvals, federal financing and government support overseas, and is proceeding despite investigations surrounding Nvidia's China sales.

title: California AG Accuses OpenAI of Misleading and Endangering the Public
summary: California's attorney general has sued OpenAI, alleging the company knowingly developed AI models without necessary safeguards and misled the public. The case is a significant state-level legal challenge to the ChatGPT maker.

title: Big Tech Needs to Spread Its Bets on Data Centers
summary: A Heard on the Street column argues that AI companies concentrating spending on a small number of mega data-center projects look exposed after the midterm elections. It makes the case for diversifying data-center bets to reduce political and execution risk.

title: Thomson Reuters CEO Says Content Is King When It Comes to AI
summary: Thomson Reuters CEO Steve Hasker says the company's proprietary content is its key advantage in AI and that it will keep investing heavily in AI-driven products. The interview reflects how information providers are positioning owned data as a moat against general-purpose AI models.

title: Verizon Trades Network Claims for Pop-Culture Buzz
summary: Under CMO Leslie Berland, who joined in 2024, Verizon has moved away from network-reliability messaging toward pop-culture-driven ads featuring TV heartthrobs, and is building an in-house team to produce ads faster. One spot was pulled after alienating viewers 55 and older, and some observers doubt buzzy ads will get customers to switch carriers.

title: Gucci Is Cutting Prices; Louis Vuitton Is Reluctant to Follow the Trend
summary: Luxury executives are openly debating price cuts to escape a three-year slump as mid-tier luxury growth has evaporated, with LVMH's CFO acknowledging internal discussions while still opposing cuts at Louis Vuitton. Gucci has already reduced prices on some items, including a bag that fell 30% from €3,500 to €2,450 in France since July.

title: Microsoft Data Shows Claude Is Stalling Against Copilot in Office
summary: Internal Microsoft data reviewed by The Information indicates that Anthropic's push to get Claude used inside Office apps has stalled relative to Microsoft's own Copilot. The report lands days before Anthropic's IPO and bears on its enterprise productivity ambitions.

title: OpenAI Explored $5 Billion–Plus Acquisition of Startup That Decodes How AI 'Thinks'
summary: OpenAI previously explored acquiring an AI interpretability startup, which works on decoding how AI models reason internally, for at least $5 billion, according to The Information. The talks highlight the rising strategic value placed on interpretability research among frontier labs.

title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Digital Wallet
summary: OpenAI announced a ChatGPT digital wallet that lets its Dot assistant make online purchases without directly accessing shoppers' card details. The move extends OpenAI's push into agentic commerce.

title: Alibaba Unveils New Flagship AI Model Qwen4-Max
summary: Alibaba added Qwen4-Max as the new flagship of its Qwen family, the world's most downloaded open-weight model series. Alibaba says it beats Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro on coding benchmarks, though unlike most Qwen models it is not open weight.

title: Nokia, Telia Target EU AI Compute Needs
summary: Nokia and Telia lead a Nordic consortium formed to build an AI gigafactory, aiming to win business under a European initiative to create a supercomputing leader. The bid positions Nordic telecom and infrastructure players in the EU's push for sovereign AI compute.

title: Millicom Inks $1.7B Deal for Entel Peru
summary: Millicom signed an agreement to buy Entel Peru for $1.7 billion including lease liabilities. The acquisition would expand the group's footprint to 13 Latin American markets.

title: FCC Tees Up April 2027 for Upper C-Band Auction
summary: The U.S. FCC will open bidding in its upper C-Band spectrum auction on April 27, 2027. Chair Brendan Carr pitched the auction as creating a 5G 'super band' unmatched by other industrialized countries.
